title: 040 transition arms: seed-rule amendment (bootstrap seed)
amends: preregistration_transition.json "seeds" ("any PASS is re-run with the HGB re-fit at random_state 1")
why: random_state alone does not perturb the stand-in on f00-f08: with early_stopping False and no feature subsampling, HistGradientBoosting uses it only for the bin-threshold subsample, taken above 200,000 fit rows (f07 172k, f08 187k, f09 203k). The rs1 tables are bit-identical to seed 1 on f00-f08 (verdicts_transition.json seed_note), so the rs1 rerun re-tested f09-f14 only.
seen_before: seed-1 and rs1 results of tr_gate / tr_scale / tr_long / tr_exit (verdicts_transition.json at ec435bc9). This amendment is written after them; it changes only how the seed-2 stand-in is drawn, not any arm, threshold, cell or rule.

seed.draw: per fold and cell, the stand-in is fit on a bootstrap resample (with replacement, same size) of that cell's fit rows, drawn from numpy default_rng([1, fold number, H, level index, direction index]); HGB random_state 1; every other setting as the seed-1 stand-in
seed.tables: user_data/data/nnmt_transition_bs1/pred_fNN.parquet (tail and test rows as seed 1; the tail percentiles come from the bootstrap model's tail predictions)
seed.arms: every seed-1 PASS (tr_scale, tr_long) re-run unchanged on these tables as <arm>_bs1

rule: the arm's own pre-registered rule applied to <arm>_bs1. A seed-1 PASS stays a PASS only if <arm>_bs1 also PASSes; otherwise 'FAIL at seed 2'. The rs1 result stays in the record as reported, not decisive.
